core_obligations: Prove (1) implies (2): represent a stalk element f_p by a triple (U, x, f) using the description of stalks, apply (1) to obtain a covering on which f or 1-f is invertible, and use that the point u maps some covering member with an element over x, so that f_p or 1-f_p is invertible (proof lines 7704-7731).
Conclude that the stalk O_p is either the zero ring or local (proof lines 7732-7741).
Under the hypothesis that the site has enough points, prove the converse by testing (1) at every point and lifting the resulting local invertibility back to a covering.
proof_roadmap: Understand stalk elements as triples (object, point-element, section).
Apply the locally ringed dichotomy on a covering and use the point property.
For the converse, globalize the pointwise statement using enough points.
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares the locally ringed condition on a ringed site with locality of the stalks at its points: the former always implies the latter, and the converse holds when the site has enough points. The proof of the implication represents an element f_p of the stalk by a triple (U, x, f), applies the locally ringed hypothesis to find a covering on which f or 1-f is invertible, and uses that the point functor u carries some member of the covering to an element mapping to x, concluding that f_p or 1-f_p is invertible (proof lines 7703-7741). The converse under the enough-points hypothesis is obtained by testing the condition at all points. H2: the manipulation of the triple description of stalks and the point-theoretic argument is the substance and is written out.
